summary: Edvard Westermarck was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (ca. 1881–1890). He held posts at the London School of Economics (ca. 1907–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (ca. 1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at University College London (ca. 1880–1882), founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society in 1914, and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and Oxford, he became Professor for Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and served at the Foreign Office (ca. 1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford, including under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian studies, he was principal at Sanskrit College (1858–1864) and held professorships at Presidency College and the University of Cambridge (1867–1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Yale and Harvard, he taught linguistics and Asian languages at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps studied at Illinois College, Yale, and the universities of Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and the East India Company College (ca. 1840–1842) before joining the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Hamburg, Cologne (Ph.D. under Max Scheler), and Bonn, also studying with Max Walleser. He held posts at the University of London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, Berkeley, and Lancaster, and vice-presided over The Buddhist Society.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (A.B.) and the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil.) before serving as Jay Professor of Greek and Latin at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross studied at UCL and Strasbourg (under Theodor Nöldeke). A specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, he held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, and served as Director of SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and under Woolsey, de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. He served as professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854) and as president of the American Oriental Society (1873–1880).

Edward Espe Brown studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Sojun Mel Weitsman, and Reb Anderson in Buddhist and religious studies. He worked as manager, cook, and Zen teacher at the San Francisco, Tassajara, and Green Gulch Farm Zen Centers between 1966 and 1980.
Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Granville Browne studied at Newcastle, Cambridge (under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell), and St Bartholomew's. A specialist in Iranian and religious studies and linguistics, he was lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He taught at UC Berkeley (ca. 1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward Hamilton Johnston studied at Eton, New College, and Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service (ca. 1909–1924) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (ca. 1937–1942).

Edward John Garrett works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche and had postdoctoral mentoring from Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Joseph Thomas studied at St Andrews under John Burnet, as well as at Cambridge. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Cambridge University Library (ca. 1909–1939) and Cambridge's Oriental Languages Department.

Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UCSB and Yale, served as dean of philosophy at Stony Brook (ca. 1978), and was president of the American Philosophical Association (2009–2010).

Edward Said studied at Victoria College, Northfield Mount Hermon, Princeton, and Harvard. Working in philosophy and literature, he served as a professor of English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from ca. 1963 to 2003.
